questions.question: A post-trip inspection should include all of the following, except:

options.text: Looking for items left on the bus.
Checking for sleeping students.
Opening windows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Opening windows.
questions.explanation: After finishing a trip, a school bus driver should inspect the bus. Check for sleeping students, belongings left behind, open windows or doors, mechanical problems, and damage.

questions.question: When alley docking, you should first:

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, drive past the alley first. Stop your vehicle parallel to the outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: Where is the overhead inside rearview mirror located?

options.text: Above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus
Above the door across from the driver
Above the emergency door in the rear

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield on the driver's side of the bus
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: A bus driver approaching a bus stop should stop at least 10 feet away from waiting students because:

options.text: The students will have to walk to the bus, so you can see their movements.
Buses are difficult to drive.
The students may get scared of the bus coming toward them.

questions.correctAnswerText: The students will have to walk to the bus, so you can see their movements.
questions.explanation: Stop the bus with the front bumper at least 10 feet from students. This makes students walk toward the bus so you can watch them.

questions.question: The overhead rearview mirror is located:

options.text: On the right side of a bus.
On the steering wheel of a bus.
Above the windshield inside a bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Above the windshield inside a bus.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror is mounted above the windshield on the driver's side. Use it to watch students inside the bus.

questions.question: Crossover mirrors help the driver see:

options.text: The front bumper danger zones.
The rear bumper.
The left side of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front bumper danger zones.
questions.explanation: Crossover mirrors show you the danger zones in front of the bus and on both sides. They show the area from the front to the service door.

questions.question: When students board a school bus, the driver should:

options.text: Read a book.
Check all mirrors.
Only look at the students.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check all mirrors.
questions.explanation: While students board, watch the loading process and check all mirrors for students running to catch the bus.

questions.question: Adjust a bus's mirrors:

options.text: Before operating the bus.
While operating the bus.
At the first stoplight after starting your shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before operating the bus.
questions.explanation: Check and adjust all mirrors before you start driving.

questions.question: If students on the bus cause a disturbance while other students are unloading, what should you do?

options.text: Immediately walk to the back of the bus and handle the disturbance while students unload.
Wait until all students are done unloading, then handle the disturbance.
Have a student who is closer to the disturbance handle it while you supervise unloading.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until all students are done unloading, then handle the disturbance.
questions.explanation: When loading or unloading students, focus completely on the process. Wait until all students have safely exited before addressing any behavior problems.

questions.question: As students exit a school bus, the driver should watch to ensure that they:

options.text: Are leaving in pairs.
Do not get caught on the handrail or door.
Do not talk while exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not get caught on the handrail or door.
questions.explanation: Students can be injured if their clothing, accessories, or bodies get caught on a handrail or door. Watch closely as students exit to make sure everyone safely leaves the bus.

questions.question: When dropping off students at a school, a driver should:

options.text: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
Leave the key in the ignition if leaving the driver's seat.
Read a book while students get off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine to secure the bus.
questions.explanation: When students get off at school, turn off the engine to secure the bus. Remove the key from the ignition if you leave your seat. Watch the students as they unload.

questions.question: When the examiner asks you to change lanes during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Change lanes right away without looking.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
Change lanes quickly, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when it is safe.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner will ask you to change lanes. Check your mirrors and blind spots first. Use your turn signal and only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When loading or unloading passengers, a school bus should be in ____ if park is not available.

options.text: Reverse
First gear
Neutral

questions.correctAnswerText: Neutral
questions.explanation: When loading or unloading students, put the bus in park if possible. If park is not available, put the bus in neutral and set the parking brake.

questions.question: If a tornado is coming and there is no shelter nearby, where should students go?

options.text: To a nearby ditch
To the closest tree
Near a river

questions.correctAnswerText: To a nearby ditch
questions.explanation: If a tornado is coming and there is no shelter, lead students to a nearby ditch or culvert. Stay away from the bus so it does not fall on them. Avoid areas with water that could flood.

questions.question: How far ahead should a school bus turn on its lights before stopping?

options.text: 2 to 4 seconds
5 to 10 seconds
45 seconds

questions.correctAnswerText: 5 to 10 seconds
questions.explanation: Turn on the amber flashing lights at least 200 feet (about 5 to 10 seconds) before you stop, unless your state law says otherwise.

questions.question: When picking up students, a school bus should:

options.text: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
Stop for students who are walking toward a bus stop.
Parents can choose where the bus stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Students should wait at a designated bus stop.
questions.explanation: Drivers can only pick up students at official stops. School officials decide where these stops are located.

questions.question: Backing a school bus is:

options.text: Strongly encouraged.
Strongly discouraged.
Only allowed in the morning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strongly discouraged.
questions.explanation: Avoid backing a school bus whenever possible. Only back up if there is no other safe way to go. Follow all safety rules if you must drive in reverse.

questions.question: When you reach railroad tracks in a school bus, you should generally:

options.text: Look at the tracks and keep driving without stopping.
Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
Stop 75 feet before the nearest rail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop 15 to 50 feet before the nearest rail.
questions.explanation: Stop before any railroad crossing. Stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail so you can see the tracks clearly. Look and listen for trains before crossing.

questions.question: When getting out of a vehicle, you must keep ____ points of contact with the vehicle at all times.

options.text: Three
Four
Two

questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Face the vehicle and keep three points of contact as you exit. If testing a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: The inside rearview mirror is used to:

options.text: Watch the passengers.
See hazards on the road.
See vehicles changing lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch the passengers.
questions.explanation: The overhead inside rearview mirror lets you watch what students are doing inside the bus.
